commit.subject: LU-18298 tests: retry the PCC backend umount in sanity-pcc
commit.message:
LU-18298 tests: retry the PCC backend umount in sanity-pcc

umount_loopdev() waits for the backend mount to go idle by polling lsof,
then umounts once. That poll cannot see what usually holds the mount:
an attached PCC inode pins it through pcci_path, and an open PCC copy
pins it through the file, and both are kernel references that belong to
no process. lsof reports the mount idle on the first iteration, the
grace loop exits immediately, and the umount fails.

cleanup_pcc_mapping() does not help here either, as lctl pcc clear frees
the dataset but detaches no inode, so any file still attached at cleanup
keeps the mount busy.

Retry the umount itself instead, dropping the client caches between
attempts. That releases the Lustre inodes and with them the PCC copies
they hold, which is what the loop was trying to wait for. Only retry
when the umount actually reported the mount busy, as zconf_umount()
does: any other failure, an already unmounted path included, comes back
the same every time and dropping the caches is system wide. Keep the
lsof call, it still reports a process holding the mount, which is the
case the old loop did handle.

This is the shape of what test_100 trips over. Its rule matches on
project ID, and projid={0} is the default one, so every file the test
touches while the mapping is registered is eligible; the mapping is
pccro=1, so it is the read loops that attach them. Whichever attachment
outlives the test, "umount: target is busy" then ends it after
everything it checks has already passed.

Fixes: 97fc40f62aa0 ("LU-10499 tests: disable metadata_csum_seed for pcc cache device")
Test-Parameters: trivial testlist=sanity-pcc
